dataset: NASA GPM IMERG precipitation - Mumbai subset
source: NASA GES DISC (Goddard Earth Sciences Data and Information Services Center)
recommended_product: GPM_3IMERGDF (IMERG Final Run, Daily, V07, 0.1deg x 0.1deg) for research-quality historical analysis; GPM_3IMERGHH (Final Run, 30-min, V07) for sub-daily storm structure
aws_open_data: https://registry.opendata.aws/nasa-gpm3imergdf/ (also on AWS S3, requires NASA Earthdata credentials via S3 bearer token, see https://data.gesdisc.earthdata.nasa.gov/s3credentialsREADME)
license: Free and open for public use (NASA data policy); attribution to NASA GES DISC requested
download_date: NOT DOWNLOADED (requires a free NASA Earthdata account - registration is instant at https://urs.earthdata.nasa.gov/users/new - and this session cannot complete interactive login or call the token-authenticated subset service; see scripts/download_imerg.py template)
format: NetCDF4/HDF5 (native), GeoTIFF (via subset service), or JSON (Giovanni timeseries API)
temporal_resolution: 30-minute (HH product) or daily (DF product); data record spans 2000-present (TRMM+GPM merged)
coverage: Recommend subsetting to Mumbai bbox (72.75-72.98E, 18.85-19.30N) via the GES DISC Simple Subset Wizard or OPeNDAP, rather than downloading global granules
file_size: a Mumbai-subset daily granule is a few KB-MB; global daily granules are much larger before subsetting
quality: high for research use (Final Run); satellite-derived, so still an estimate rather than a gauge
limitations: Requires free Earthdata login (instant approval). 0.1deg resolution is coarser than the city itself, similar caveat to ERA5.
notes: Per task instructions: prioritize a few representative historical heavy-rainfall events (e.g. 26-27 July 2005, and recent 2017/2019/2021/2024 Mumbai monsoon flood dates) rather than downloading the full global archive. Exact event date list should be finalized against flood_observations records once available.
